title: Hall Taco Bar Night
seoTitle: Hall Taco Bar Night | Firefighter Meal
subtitle: Build-your-own tacos at the table
description: Build-your-own tacos at the table. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Hall Taco Bar Night in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch beef. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Prep toppings
steps.instruction: Dice onion, pick cilantro leaves, cut limes into wedges. Warm a sheet tray for holding cooked protein — tacos move fast once meat hits the board.

steps.title: Cook the filling
steps.instruction: Season protein with salt and cumin. Sear over medium-high until cooked through (chicken 165°F, steak 130°F then rest). Rest steak 8 minutes; slice thin against the grain.

steps.title: Warm tortillas
steps.instruction: Char tortillas on a dry griddle 20 seconds per side or wrap in foil at 300°F 10 minutes. Stack in a towel so they stay pliable. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 145°F for medium beef, 160°F for ground. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Hall Taco Bar Night onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 8 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Run the taco line
steps.instruction: Hall Taco Bar Night: protein, onion, cilantro, lime. Crew builds their own — fastest way to feed eight without cold plates. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Final quality check before service
steps.instruction: Walk the line once before opening service for Hall Taco Bar Night — confirm hotel pans are labeled, backup trays are in the 200°F oven, and thermometers are calibrated. Rookies should ask a senior cook to spot-check the first portion.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Label every topping bowl — rookies grab faster when they can read the line.
Keep hot bases (potatoes, chips) in cambros at 200°F and cold toppings on ice if service runs long.
Put forks, napkins, and a trash can at the end of the bar — self-serve feeds get messy fast.
Line up Hall Taco Bar Night on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Build-your-own tacos at the table. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
mealPrepNotes: Prep mise en place before the shift — Hall Taco Bar Night runs smoother when proteins are trimmed, spices are pre-measured, and hotel pans are labeled before the first tone.
